newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Murder suspect gets high votes in Sri Lanka poll.
newsitem.headline: Murder suspect gets high votes in Sri Lanka poll.

text.p: A key suspect in the killing of a Sri Lankan ruling coalition legislator, which sparked riots in a southeastern town last month, has polled the most votes in an election for the town's council.

Mahinda Ratnatilleke, the main opposition United National Party's (UNP) mayoral candidate for the gem-mining town of Ratnapura, 80 km (50 miles) southeast of the capital Colombo, garnered the most votes in the March 21 local council polls.
Ratnatilleke received 8,326 votes to 4,596 for the leading People's Alliance (PA) candidate, the Elections Department said. The PA, however, won 10 seats on the municipal council to the UNP's five.

Only a few weeks ago, posters denouncing Ratnatilleke sprang up all over Ratnapura after police issued a warrant for his arrest in connection with the killing of ruling PA legislator Nalanda Ellawela in a shootout.
Ratnatilleke, a former UNP mayor of the town, and UNP legislator Susantha Punchinilame are among several suspects in police custody in connection with the killing.
Ratnatilleke conducted his campaign from jail.
The killing sparked riots in Ratnapura as PA supporters went on a rampage, burning houses and shops.
It also became part of the PA's campaign rhetoric as the government promised to end Sri Lanka's gun culture and launched a crackdown on illegal firearms.
